text:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT 4970001111] kvcache memory climb detected on hosted-runtime cluster us-west-2. Severity: high. Observed sustained GPU mem > 92% across a subset of pods. Auto-escalating to on-call.

alex: I see the alert. spike started ~10m ago, correlates with a backlog of long-context requests to model-redwood-llama-70b.

maria: noted. any recent deploys to continuous-batching or prefetch?

devon: we rolled batching-window=120ms -> 250ms in rollout yesterday for throughput; there was also a prefetch tweak to increase lookahead cache size. rolling back now?

carla: customer impact: support queue shows increased 503s and slow tails for a handful of customers hitting long prompts (>50k tokens). Ticket #SR-8732 flagged latency/timeouts.

oncall-sre: I'm on pager. grabbing flamegraphs and kvmap snapshots. can someone drop non-critical prefetch jobs?

alex: doing a live config rollback for batching-window to 120ms (canary first). command: `rctl deploy rollback continuous-batching --target canary --reason "kvcache mem spike"`

incident-bot: Deployment rollback started by alex. Canary will be 2 pods.

maria: also toggling prefetch: set prefetch.max_session_kv=4096 -> 1024 to limit per-session prefetch. doing hotpatch: `curl -X POST https://infra/api/flags -d '{"prefetch.max_session_kv":1024}'`

devon: patch applied to canaries. watching memory.

oncall-sre: memory trending down on canaries, good sign. but some older sessions still have huge kv maps; eviction not keeping up. we should trigger a controlled session eviction on affected nodes.

carla: preparing customer comms: impacted customers are org-omega, acme-intel; severity page/priority: P1 for those SLAs.

support-lead: I'll open rapid response thread with those customers and offer guidance on reducing prompt context while we mitigate.

alex: immediate mitigation actions list:
- rollback batching-window to previous value (in progress)
- reduce prefetch max per-session to 1024 (done on canaries, rolling)
- enable aggressive kv eviction on affected hosts: `kvctl set-evict-policy --age 30m --min-keep 128`
- soft-restart long-lived sessions older than 2h on targeted pods

maria: eviction policy pushed to all pods now. logs show evictions:
```
[2026-03-15T04:12:42Z] evicting session s=abc123 size=16284 entries=18
[2026-03-15T04:12:43Z] evicting session s=def456 size=14490 entries=16
```

devon: restarting long-lived sessions on three affected nodes (rolling restart to keep capacity): `kubectl rollout restart deployment/hosted-runtime -n prod --selector=kvnode=hot-0`

oncall-sre: restart in progress. note: restarts will drop in-flight requests; routing will fallback to smaller-model variants for a short window. set fallback policy to allow model-redwood-llama-13b for latency-sensitive routes.

carla: support update: customers informed about temporary degraded performance and mitigation steps. asking for any urgent jobs to be paused.

incident-bot: Canary rollback completed. Fleet rollback 0/6 -> 6/6 in progress.

alex: fleet rollback done. memory now at 70-75% across the fleet. prefetch cap rolled out to all clusters. we're observing reduced new kv allocations.

maria: follow-up: we should add a guard to the prefetch controller to back off when average kvmap growth rate > 100MB/min per pod. file for follow-up PR.

devon: root cause hypothesis: batching-window increase + larger prefetch window caused longer-lived KV caches to accumulate per-request prefix expansion on long prompts; combined with a small subset of clients sending extreme context append sequences, we hit OOMs.

oncall-sre: confirming. reproducer found in test harness: simulate many 60k-token prefix sessions with prefetch=8192 causes kvmap growth leading to mem cliff. will add automated test to CI.

carla: Customer impact recap for postmortem: ~4 customers experienced 5-20% error rates for ~18 minutes, highest tail latency 2.5x SLA for a subset of calls. No data loss. Communicated remediation and plan.

support-lead: created postmortem ticket PM-4970001111 and assigned follow-ups: telemetry alert thresholds, prefetch rate-limiter, batching-window rollout guard, customer escalation playbook updates.

alex: immediate follow-ups (owners):
- telemetry thresholds and alert tuning (maria)
- prefetch controller backoff and per-session hard cap (devon)
- rollout safety gate for batching-window changes (alex)
- postmortem writeup + customer comms (carla)

maria: I'm drafting the alert rule: trigger when pod_kvmap_growth_bytes_per_min > 100*1024*1024 for 3m AND gpu_mem_usage > 85%.

devon: PR for prefetch cap + backoff in review: `git/infra#4212` adds a per-customer circuit-breaker and test.

oncall-sre: closing page. resource pressure returned to normal. leaving notes in incident channel and marking for postmortem.

carla: thanks team. I'll schedule a cross-functional postmortem review tomorrow 09:30 PT.

alex: thumbs. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT 4970001111 status: resolved -> monitoring. duration: ~42m. owners set.

carla: adding final timeline to PM ticket now.

maria: added CI test and a short-term kill-switch flag for prefetch in case of recurrence.

devon: moving the batching-window change behind a canary-only rollout by default.

support-lead: Customer follow-ups queued; will share final note after PM complete.

oncall-sre: signing off.

alex: closing thread, will follow up in postmortem doc.
